newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON ONLY FIFTH IN BRITISH 200M RACE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON ONLY FIFTH IN BRITISH 200M RACE.

text.p: Michael Johnson, the 200 metres world record holder and Olympic champion, was comprehensively beaten over the distance in a low key athletics challenge meeting at Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Johnson, running for an international select team, finished only fifth in a pedestrian time of 20.87, one-and-a-half seconds outside his world record 19.32, as veteran Welshman Doug Turner claimed an unexpected victory.
Turner, 31, recorded 20.73 to edge Marcus Adam by a hundredth. Julian Golding completed a British clean sweep in 20.80.
"I wasn't sure if Johnson was running and I didn't even run a particularly good race," said Turner.
There were no problems for the 100 metres world record holder Donovan Bailey who cruised to victory in the short sprint in 10.13.
American Vince Henderson was second in 10.22 with British teenage sensation Dwain Chambers third (10.31).
Bailey, who struggled with illness and injury during the world championships where he won silver, said he was using Sunday's meeting to decide on his near future.
"I basically judged whether to compete for the rest of the season on what I did here," said the Canadian Olympic champion.
"In Athens I caught a stomach virus, lost 14 lbs and couldn't really train. I had some injury problems that I don't want to talk about right now but I've had to deal with them and I felt fine today."

The 110 metres hurdles was billed as another showdown between Britons Colin Jackson and Tony Jarrett but a mix-up in the race schedule meant Jarrett, who beat his old rival in Zurich last Wednesday, could not take part. That left Jackson, silver medallist in the world championships, to cruise to an easy win in 13.21.
John Godina, America's world shot putt champion who also finished fifth in the discus in Athens, again showed his versatility by completing a double victory.
A throw of 64.32 metres beat British veteran Bob Weir by 10 centimetres in the discus while 21.75m, a British all-comers' record, was enough to win the shot.

Surprise world champion Marius Corbett of South Africa again got the better of local favourite Steve Backley to win the javelin with a throw of 87.46. Backley, second to Corbett in Athens, took the same position on Sunday with 87.14.
London-based Australian world champion Cathy Freeman won the women's 400 metres in 50.61, holding off a determined challenge from Briton Allison Curbishly (51.04).
Iwan Thomas took the men's event in 44.69, with 1991 world champion American Antonio Pettigrew (44.84) holding off Mark Richardson (45.10) for second.
Jonathan Edwards' poor triple jump form continued as he finished behind fellow Briton Francis Agyepong for the second time in a week.
Edwards, who lost his world title in Athens, had not been beaten by another Briton since 1994 until Agyepong beat him in Zurich on Wednesday and was out of sorts again at Crystal Palace.
Agyepong won with 16.72, four centimetres ahead of the world record holder.
